title: Lp functions with exponent at least one are locally integrable
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field] and Lebesgue measure on $\mathbf R^m$, $m\geq1$. Let $1\leq p<\infty$ and let $f:\mathbf R^m\to\mathbf C$ be measurable with finite $L^p$ norm $\|f\|_p=(\int |f(x)|^p\,dx)^{1/p}$. Then $f$ is locally integrable: every point has a neighborhood on which $\int|f(x)|\,dx$ is finite.
